title: Resident Johan von Lilienthal in Moscow, 1665-1667 (Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Muscovitica 1/36/82): key of the homophonic German letter code rebuilt from the contemporary glosses and validated

transcription.notes: Held-out part of the key test: lines 1-10 of the left page (185 groups), transcribed after the key was frozen, then the gloss read; the first 160 groups were measured.

system.summary: German letter substitution with homophones, 2-3 digit groups separated by dots, mixed with clear German; numbers also for ch, sch, st, ss, ll, ff and tz; u = v = w. Six code series (23-59, 63-100, 103-150, 153-190, 293-349, 353-390), each in alphabetical order; numbers ending in 1 or 2 do not occur; 293-349 repeats the order of 23-59 and 353-390 that of 63-100. 107-120 and 303-320 never seen.

prior_solution.where: The German glosses written between the lines over the code runs at the time are a decipherment, on every page checked (ours: bands through 28-49, 38, 42, 45 and 47 more fully; Daniel Bourdeau's leads review n09 of 6 Nov 2026: 31, 42, 45 at 2600 px, after the sweep's 38 and 47), so the content is not new. No printed key or edition found (leads review n09: nothing on DECODE, at Cryptiana or in Lasry's lists); no target, branch or PR for Lilienthal or R0000814 in this repository (GitHub API, 10 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau's Riksarkivet sweep found the volume and his leads review n09 (6 Nov 2026) vetted it as lead 2316 ('read': glossed group by group). Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol and key frozen before a single held-out measurement, thresholds fixed in advance). AI agents transcribed, built the key, measured and wrote up. No human palaeographer checked the transcription.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Images 42 (both pages) and 47 (left): 97 glossed runs (cipher groups with the gloss over them) read from the 3000 px IIIF images.

Key of 158 codes learned from the glossed runs of images 42 and 47 only, without a conflict on 1116 aligned groups; frozen by SHA-256 with the amended protocol before the held-out page was looked at closely. (A first protocol, which took the code for a nomenclator and held out image 42, was amended before any measurement.)

One measurement on image 45, left page (first 160 groups of lines 1-10, transcribed after the freeze, gloss read after the numbers): 0.887 of characters against 0.047 for the best of 200 shuffled keys (mean 0.024); margin 0.840; thresholds >= 0.85 and margin >= 0.30, fixed in advance.

Gloss inventory: bands at 3000 px through the middle of every page 28-49 and 38 right in full: a gloss over every run seen (the Latin words of 38 are enciphered letter by letter and glossed); no bare passage found (agrees with leads review n09). The decode of image 45 shows the gloss sometimes summarises (cipher 'haten auch etliche', gloss 'und welche').

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was learned from the contemporary interlinear decipherment (glosses) of images 42 and 47 and validated once on image 45. The content is the glosses' (existing); the key is the contribution.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): amended protocol and key hashed before the held-out page was looked at closely; one measurement on image 45 left (160 groups, 168 decoded positions): 0.887 of characters vs best of 200 shuffled keys 0.047 (mean 0.024), margin 0.840. Threshold fixed in advance: >= 0.85 and margin >= 0.30. Later additions (89 st, 27 ff, 64 c, 54 tz, 348 z and rows from the table's order) are derived after the measurement and not tested.

texts.label: Image 45, left page, lines 1-10: the held-out cipher groups with the contemporary gloss
texts.note: A cipher passage from mid-sentence to mid-sentence, broken by two short clear insertions that are not transcribed: our decode with key.tsv beside the gloss written at the time. The gloss is the reading of the time, but it summarises in places.
texts.summary: Someone holds firmly to his instruction and secret propositions; some of the great boyars, Dolgoruka, Ilia Danielewitz and Almasi, talked it over together after yesterday's conference and let it be known that ...

reading_review.note: decode read against the contemporary gloss as German phrases; agrees except where the gloss summarises (haten auch etliche / und welche; feste auff / hatte auf), gehanen/geheimen and spellings; a fragment of a letter, the clear text between the runs not transcribed; one reader

outcome.notes: The letters were deciphered at the time (interlinear glosses on every page checked), so we claim no reading and no solution; what is new is the key as a reusable table, validated on a held-out page. Sibling target ebers1664 (lead 2315, PR #383) is the code of the commissary Adolf Ebers, a different code.
